title: Computer Numerically Controlled Tool Programmers
description: Develop programs to control machining or processing of materials by automatic machine tools, equipment, or systems. May also set up, operate, or maintain equipment.

tasks.text: Determine the sequence of machine operations, and select the proper cutting tools needed to machine workpieces into the desired shapes.
Analyze job orders, drawings, blueprints, specifications, printed circuit board pattern films, and design data to calculate dimensions, tool selection, machine speeds, and feed rates.
Observe machines on trial runs or conduct computer simulations to ensure that programs and machinery will function properly and produce items that meet specifications.
Write programs in the language of a machine's controller and store programs on media, such as punch tapes, magnetic tapes, or disks.
Determine reference points, machine cutting paths, or hole locations, and compute angular and linear dimensions, radii, and curvatures.
Enter computer commands to store or retrieve parts patterns, graphic displays, or programs that transfer data to other media.
Revise programs or tapes to eliminate errors, and retest programs to check that problems have been solved.
Modify existing programs to enhance efficiency.
Enter coordinates of hole locations into program memories by depressing pedals or buttons of programmers.
Sort shop orders into groups to maximize materials utilization and minimize machine setup time.
Compare encoded tapes or computer printouts with original part specifications and blueprints to verify accuracy of instructions.
Prepare geometric layouts from graphic displays, using computer-assisted drafting software or drafting instruments and graph paper.
Perform preventative maintenance or minor repairs on machines.
Write instruction sheets and cutter lists for a machine's controller to guide setup and encode numerical control tapes.
Align and secure pattern film on reference tables of optical programmers, and observe enlarger scope views of printed circuit boards.

skills.name: Computer aided design CAD software
skills.def: Software to design 2D or 3D objects. May include engineering or architectural features. Examples: Autodesk AutoCAD, Dassault Systemes CATIA, Dassault Systemes SolidWorks, PTC Creo Parametric.

skills.name: Computer aided manufacturing CAM software
skills.def: Software to control machine tools which fabricate or assemble objects. Examples: 1CadCam Unigraphics, 3D Systems GibbsCAM, Autodesk Fusion 360, Autodesk PartMaker.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: G-code, M-code.

skills.name: Enterprise resource planning ERP software
skills.def: Software to integrate, monitor, or analyze data from multiple business operations within a unified system. Examples: Aptean Made2Manage, SAP software.

skills.name: Enterprise application integration software
skills.def: Software to connect different business systems to improve scalability or streamline work flows. Examples: Extensible markup language XML.
